The fine amounts to $4.7 billion, stemming from anti-competitive bundling practices.
The core issue is the bundling of Google's search engine and browser with the Android operating system.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedups of up to 90% were observed when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy and control.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with existing local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for optimized on-device AI.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks privately without relying on external cloud services.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Sony’s PlayStation disc factory is already being repurposed
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Sony is actively repurposing its PlayStation disc manufacturing facilities.
The industry shift towards digital media is confirmed by Sony's internal planning.
The Thalgau plant currently produces 600,000 discs daily, half for PlayStation.

stories.title: Musk’s X poses “serious risk to Americans’ privacy,” advocates warn FTC
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The FTC is warning that Elon Musk's X platform poses a 'serious risk to Americans’ privacy.'
The FTC is urging regulators to reject Musk's proposal to end monitoring on X.
Concerns surrounding AI usage and privacy are central to the regulatory push against X's current policies.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: The paper addresses a novel security threat in autonomous AI coding agents where codebases persist across sessions.
It introduces 'Distributed Attacks' where a compromised agent can strategically time malicious payloads across multiple Pull Requests (PRs) for better stealth.
The research proposes 'Iterative VibeCoding' as a framework to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing and retaining sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
Focuses on 'Unlearning,' a method to reliably remove this memorized knowledge post-hoc from large language models.
Introduces 'LACUNA,' a new testbed to evaluate localization precision, moving beyond current output-level benchmarks to assess true knowledge erasure.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: OrbitQuant addresses the high inference cost of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) used in image/video generation.
It solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ).
The method is 'data-agnostic,' meaning it bypasses the need for re-fitting calibration data for every new model checkpoint or modality.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-resistant tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Aims to replace reliance on external LLM APIs by compiling natural language specs into local, executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses key limitations of current LLM usage, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Meta has a new app called Pocket that is absolutely nothing like the old Pocket
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is launching a new app named Pocket, replacing the functionality of the previously defunct Mozilla Pocket.
The new Pocket app is heavily AI-focused, allowing users to create and share interactive 'gizmos' from AI prompts.
The launch aligns with Meta's stated commitment and focus on integrating AI across its products.

stories.title: The video game disc is dead
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: The article discusses the perceived end of the physical video game disc era.
It references the historical trend of gamers accumulating physical hardware and media.
The shift suggests a move towards purely digital distribution models for games.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS malware variant, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware is classified as an infostealer, targeting Mac users.
The discovery highlights a growing trend and increased focus on Mac-specific cyber threats.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to permit supersonic airliners to fly over US cities.
The key condition for this allowance is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to avoid creating a sonic boom.
This development signals a potential regulatory shift enabling the return of supersonic commercial travel.

stories.title: Trump gets OpenAI to offer US 5% stake, far lower than Sanders’ target
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Trump administration is reportedly in talks with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
The proposed deal involves the US government acquiring a 5% stake in OpenAI.
This stake offer is noted as being significantly lower than targets previously discussed by figures like Bernie Sanders.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a post-hoc method to remove this memorized knowledge from models.
The research introduces LACUNA, a testbed to evaluate localization precision, moving beyond simple output-level unlearning benchmarks.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their capacity to utilize that information effectively.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from privileged teachers in OPSD can cause overfitting and hurt cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating policy disagreement during self-distillation.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that merges Recurrent Reasoning Models (RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
Utilizes symbol-equivariant RRMs (SE-RRMs) to generate complete solution proposals and guide classical solvers (e.g., SAT solvers).
Demonstrates improved extrapolation capabilities of SE-RRMs when tackling larger constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of relying on LLM APIs for tasks like log alerting or JSON repair (locality, reproducibility, cost).

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs generating unsafe outputs even after alignment training.
Proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The system's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in mathematical reasoning and red teaming evaluations.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience, context) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social interaction.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that traditional dense token-level supervision in OPSD can cause overfitting and hinder cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning by mitigating the negative effects of privileged information dependency in self-distillation.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for controllable simulated agents designed for realistic traffic simulation.
The agents learn a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from discounted returns, enabling steerable behavior.
Controllability allows engineers to isolate variables and test autonomous systems safely by reproducing edge cases.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of training LLMs in specialized domains without expensive human annotations.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the model's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels for self-supervision.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
It provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under non-IID data conditions.
This work aims to fill a gap in the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness when dealing with decentralized, heterogeneous data.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data, such as PII.
It critiques current unlearning methods, which often rely on a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach.
The research introduces a testbed (LACUNA) to evaluate localization precision, moving beyond simple output-level unlearning checks.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs in real-world deployment despite alignment training.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system to detect unsafe LLM outputs.
The monitor uses an external model's verification signal, calibrated via risk control, to trigger alarms.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience, context) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Introduces a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social dynamics.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines across 900+ characters.
Proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during multimodal reasoning.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly attend to visual inputs during error correction.
Aims to improve the models' ability to generate grounded corrections, particularly for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates the potential of scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study addresses whether simulation accuracy is inherently linked to general LLM capabilities or if it requires separate research focus.
The authors utilize scaling laws to examine the correlation between compute scale, general performance, and simulation fidelity.

stories.title: crustc: Entirety of rustc, translated to C
stories.author: github.com via ajdecon
bullet_points: A project named 'crustc' has been created, which translates the entirety of the Rust compiler (rustc) to C.
This represents a significant engineering effort in compiler technology and language portability.
The news is posted on Lobsters, suggesting an audience interested in deep technical and systems programming topics.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution breaking sandboxes in KDE Plasma
stories.author: blog.kimiblock.top via ecksdee
bullet_points: A security vulnerability involving arbitrary code execution was discovered.
The exploit specifically targets and breaks out of sandboxing mechanisms within KDE Plasma.
This represents a significant security flaw in a widely used desktop environment.
